reason: net44 is only connected to C0 (VOUT1–net44) and R2 (net44–VSS), forming a secondary RC to ground. If you remove R2, net44 becomes a floating capacitor node, effectively eliminating that auxiliary compensation/load path without changing the DC biasing of the amplifier.
impact_estimate: Low–Moderate: DC operating point largely unchanged; AC stability/phase margin may change if that RC was intended as compensation or load emulation.

reason: C0 participates only in the RC branch with R2 and does not set any transistor bias conditions. Removing it mainly affects frequency response (compensation, filtering, or load capacitance emulation) while keeping core differential amplification intact.
impact_estimate: Low–Moderate: Gain/offset largely unchanged; transient response and stability may degrade depending on whether C0 was required for compensation.

reason: R3 is a shunt load from the output to ground; deleting it simply reduces the output’s DC/AC loading, which typically does not break the amplifier core operation. The amplifier will generally still function, just with different output swing/loading conditions.
impact_estimate: Low: Output bias current and small-signal loading change; measured gain may increase and output operating point may shift slightly if the design relied on R3 as a defined load.
